messages:
clare: Noticing a recurring instability: newly provisioned shards often look like the lowest-latency option and then spike. Want to avoid ad-hoc fixes. Thoughts on a principled dampening in the policy engine?
akshay: Data shows most wins happen within first 3-5 minutes with sample_count < 10. Probabilistic hedging or a shrinkage penalty could help.
tess: Prefer shrinkage (move small-n p95 toward global prior) + small entropy floor so nothing looks impossibly fast. Also consider short-lived admit_tokens to let shards warm.
sam: Implementation note: add runtime primitives: shrinkage(p95, n, prior_bucket), entropy_floor(min_score), admit_tokens(k, ttl). Keep DSL unchanged and expose tenant override for opt-in.
routing-bot: FYI I can emit sample_count and prior_bucket per shard for last 30d.
clare: Quick experiment plan: 1) sim with shrinkage+floor vs current (48h), 2) shadow scoring 1w, 3) canary admit_tokens k=2 on 1% traffic. Monitor selection-regret and cost-per-token.
akshay: Ops risk: raising floor biases to expensive capacity. Mitigate with conservative defaults and per-tenant mode {conservative, default, aggressive}.
tess: We'll document rationale in policy FAQ to avoid product confusion. sam, can you prototype primitives this sprint?
sam: Yep, filing GH tasks now. I'll also add telemetry hooks.
clare: Action items: runtime primitives (sam), sims (akshay), docs/FAQ (tess), dashboard+alerts (clare). Sync next arch check-in. :white_check_mark:
